findings.title: SQL feature gate contains inverted dead logic and always returns false
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions), then returns false both when enabled is true and when it is false. The feature-flag value therefore has no effect, the variable name and negation misrepresent the security intent, and the function unnecessarily dereferences h.features even though it can never return true; a reader constructed without feature toggles would panic on a SQL query instead of cleanly rejecting it. Replace this with an unconditional return false (with a comment explaining SQL expressions are disabled) or remove the helper and reject directly at the call site.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand entry point is not explicitly disabled
findings.body: The explicit SQL-expression rejection is added only to ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery in pkg/expr/reader.go, while UnmarshalSQLCommand here still accepts a SQL expression and forwards it to NewSQLCommand. It is currently blocked only incidentally because the stubbed sql.TablesList/RunCommands returns 'not implemented', producing a misleading 'error reading SQL command' BadRequest; there is no explicit disabled check or feature/feature-toggle awareness on this path. If the in-memory DB implementation is later restored, this entry point silently becomes functional again without passing through the reader.go gate. Reject SQL commands explicitly on this unmarshalling path as defense-in-depth.

findings.title: No regression tests cover the disabled SQL-expression behavior
findings.body: This security change makes RunCommands and QueryFramesInto always return 'not implemented', makes pkg/expr/sql.TablesList always fail, makes NewSQLCommand always fail, and makes the reader reject QueryTypeSQL, but the PR changes no _test.go files. Existing tests that expect table parsing or SQL execution to succeed will now fail or need skipping, and there is no new regression test proving a SQL expression is rejected even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled (the CVE scenario) via both the reader path and UnmarshalSQLCommand. Add/update tests asserting the disabled behavior so a future refactor of enableSqlExpressions or the DB stub cannot silently re-enable the vulnerable path.
